The National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) has selected 317 women entrepreneurs for its IgniteHER Boot Camp Cohort 3, as part of efforts to strengthen women-led businesses, improve access to investment and expand technology-driven entrepreneurship in Nigeria.
The participants, drawn from the North-West, North-East, South-East and South-South geopolitical zones, are expected to receive training in digital innovation, business development, investment readiness and strategies for scaling their enterprises.
Speaking at the virtual opening ceremony of the programme on Sunday, NITDA Director-General, Kashifu Inuwa, said the initiative was designed to help women entrepreneurs transform innovative ideas into sustainable businesses capable of attracting funding and creating jobs.
He said the programme was aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, particularly its emphasis on human capital development, economic inclusion and innovation.
According to him, IgniteHER is intended to provide practical business support and connect women founders with opportunities to grow beyond the early stages of entrepreneurship.
The first two cohorts trained 220 women, while the second edition featured an intensive two-week hybrid boot camp involving 111 participants in August 2025.
Inuwa said some beneficiaries had recorded measurable progress, including seven women entrepreneurs who gained international exposure in Japan, with one of them, Kemisola Bolarinwa of NextWare Technologies, subsequently securing $500,000 in equity funding from WhiteStat Ventures.
He said the experience demonstrated the importance of connecting entrepreneurs to investment networks, mentorship and international markets.
The NITDA chief urged participants to focus on developing solutions to real-world problems, understanding their customers and building sustainable businesses, rather than viewing the programme as another training exercise or opportunity to obtain certificates.
He said the agency would strengthen the link between IgniteHER and its Idea Hatch incubation programme to provide mentorship, investment readiness and market access for founders, particularly those with minimum viable products in healthcare, agriculture, finance and fashion.
Inuwa added that NITDA was working towards expanding the programme across all six geopolitical zones, with the ultimate goal of reaching entrepreneurs in the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.
He said the success of the initiative would be measured by business growth, investment secured, markets accessed and jobs created, rather than the number of participants trained.
The agency, he added, was also exploring seed funding mechanisms to support promising founders, while urging implementing partners, including the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), to document beneficiaries’ progress and ensure the programme delivers long-term economic impact.
Representing JICA, Ayumi Sato urged the participants to approach the boot camp as the beginning of a demanding entrepreneurial journey, encouraging them to learn from mentors, collaborate with one another and remain open to challenging existing business assumptions.
She said the diversity of backgrounds, experiences and ideas among the participants could strengthen the programme and help them develop innovative solutions to business and societal challenges.
Sato noted that beneficiaries of previous cohorts had secured grants and initiated discussions with investors, demonstrating the value of practical training and professional networks in supporting women-led businesses.
She urged the entrepreneurs to apply the knowledge gained after the programme, stressing that the real work of building sustainable businesses would begin when the boot camp ended.
The Lead Facilitator of IgniteHER Cohort 3, Nnamdi Nwachukwu, said the initiative was designed to strengthen digital innovation and entrepreneurship capabilities, prepare women-led startups for venture financing and improve their capacity to engage investors.
He said the programme would also build a pipeline of women-led, technology-enabled businesses capable of scaling and contributing to Nigeria’s economic development.
With hubs in Rivers, Kano, Jigawa and Enugu states, the boot camp is expected to help participants refine their business models, strengthen their investment readiness and position their enterprises for growth.
